title: sprite.ts: text-with-filters PlaceObject3 drops instanceName in symbol timelines
description: In packages/swf/src/sprite.ts, when a TextDisplayObject with filters is placed in a symbol timeline (the sprite compiler path), lines 330 and 433 call encodePlaceObject3WithFilters without passing the instanceName. This means text fields with filters inside movie clips lose their AS2 instance name: _root.myMc.myTextField.text = 'x' silently fails because PlaceObject3 has HasName=0. The fix in compile.ts (main timeline, line 1812-1820) correctly passes textName to encodePlaceObject3WithFilters, but sprite.ts never picks up displayObj.instanceName for the text+filters path. The non-filter text path in sprite.ts goes to encodePlaceObject2ForText which also drops the name (line 343) — but that is a pre-existing limitation. The regression here is that adding a filter to a named text field inside a symbol timeline silently strips the name. Fix: extract instanceName from displayObj at lines 330 and 433 in sprite.ts and pass it as the name arg, mirroring the compile.ts fix.
